how_to_use: Start with the guide chapters in order. Set up the workbook sheets with your own items and supplier costs. Run the two week waste log. Hold the first variance review using the agenda template. Repeat weekly.
limitations: Designed for single-unit independent restaurants. Not built for multi-unit consolidation, commissary production, catering banquets, or bar and liquor inventory. Spreadsheet has no live supplier price feed. Waste log relies on honest staff recording.
long_description: A practical food cost control kit for independent restaurants: count sheets, a recipe coster, a variance dashboard, a two week waste log, and par reorder sheets, plus a weekly review routine that ties them together. You compute actual usage from opening inventory plus purchases minus closing inventory, compare it against theoretical cost from recipes, and investigate the gap each week. Illustrative examples show each formula step by step.
name: Restaurant Food Cost Control Kit
outcome_statement: Run a steady weekly routine that measures theoretical versus actual food cost, records waste, and keeps pars current.
problem_statement: Many independent restaurants run 28 to 35 percent food cost with thin margins. Without a routine, over-portioning, spoilage, and untracked waste leak profit quietly week after week.
short_description: Weekly food cost control kit for independent restaurants: inventory sheets, recipe coster, variance dashboard, waste log, and par reorder discipline.
support: Email support for file access and formula questions. Response within two business days. Custom menu costing and on-site training are not included.
whats_included: Workbook spreadsheet with 5 sheets: Inventory Count, Recipe Coster, Variance Dashboard, Waste Log, Par Reorder
3 print-ready templates: Weekly Review Agenda, Recipe Cost Card, Waste Log Sheet
